name: Exelon

summary.text: Exelon Corporation is a Chicago-based utility holding company. In September 2009 its chief executive John Rowe announced that Exelon would let its U.S. Chamber of Commerce membership lapse because of the Chamber's opposition to climate legislation. In July 2020 its Illinois utility Commonwealth Edison (ComEd) entered a deferred prosecution agreement with federal prosecutors and agreed to pay $200 million over a scheme to arrange jobs and contracts for associates of a high-level Illinois official in order to influence legislation; the bribery charge was dismissed in July 2023 after ComEd complied with the agreement. In February 2022 Exelon separated its power-generation business, including the largest U.S. nuclear fleet, into the independent company Constellation.

sources.title: Commonwealth Edison Agrees to Pay $200 Million to Resolve Federal Criminal Investigation

facts.claim: In September 2009 Exelon chief executive John Rowe announced, in a keynote at the American Council for an Energy-Efficient Economy conference in Chicago, that Exelon would let its U.S. Chamber of Commerce membership lapse, citing the Chamber's efforts to fight legislation to curb global warming; Exelon was the third energy company in a week to break with the Chamber, after Pacific Gas & Electric and PNM Resources.

facts.claim: On July 17, 2020 the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Illinois announced that Commonwealth Edison had agreed to pay $200 million to resolve a federal criminal investigation into a years-long bribery scheme, admitting it arranged jobs, vendor subcontracts and payments for associates of a high-level Illinois official to influence and reward the official's efforts on legislation affecting ComEd; prosecutors filed a one-count bribery information and agreed to defer prosecution for three years.
facts.quote: ComEd admits arranging jobs and contracts for political allies of a high-level State of Illinois official

facts.claim: The ComEd filing described the conduct as beginning around 2011 and continuing through around 2019 and referred to 'Public Official A', who controlled which measures were called for a vote in the Illinois House; the U.S. Attorney declined to identify the official, and Illinois House Speaker Michael Madigan, who was not charged at that time, denied wrongdoing.

facts.claim: Exelon chief executive Christopher Crane said in response to the ComEd agreement that some of ComEd's past lobbying practices and interactions with public officials did not live up to the company's commitments.

sources.title: ComEd to pay $200M in federal bribery investigation; Illinois House Speaker Mike Madigan implicated in charge

facts.claim: On July 17, 2023 a federal judge in Chicago dismissed the bribery charge against ComEd after prosecutors told the court the company had fully complied with the terms of the deferred prosecution agreement; four former ComEd officials had been convicted months earlier of attempting to corruptly influence Madigan.

facts.claim: In early February 2022 Exelon completed the separation of its competitive generation and retail business, which became the independent, Nasdaq-listed company Constellation (ticker CEG) and holds the nation's largest fleet of nuclear plants; Exelon shareholders received one Constellation share for every three Exelon shares, and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission had approved the licence transfers in 2021.

openQuestions: Site claim that ComEd paid $200 million under a deferred-prosecution agreement over a scheme to buy influence with Speaker Madigan is supported by the DOJ release and WTTW; the DOJ filing itself referred only to 'Public Official A'.
Site claims that Madigan was convicted in 2025, sentenced to 7.5 years and that the Seventh Circuit upheld the conviction in April 2026 were not tested in this pass.
Site lobby-section claim that 'Apple, PG&E and Exelon quit the Chamber in 2009 over its climate stance' is supported for Exelon and PG&E by the sources opened; Apple's departure was not checked.

The task asked about an 'Exelon ALEC exit'. No source found reports Exelon leaving ALEC; the 2009 departure was from the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, and the utilities reported to have left ALEC were American Electric Power, Xcel Energy, MidAmerican, Alliant and PG&E. The owner should treat any Exelon-ALEC claim as unsupported unless a source is found.
The sources opened do not state in terms that ComEd is an Exelon subsidiary, although Exelon's chief executive answered for the agreement; the owner may wish to add an SEC filing.
